purpose: Evaluate whether unrelated UI outputs derive their visual systems from product context instead of converging on one model-default template.

prompts: Design an emergency dispatch console for expert operators handling concurrent incidents.
Design a small ceramics store centered on material, scale, provenance, and shipping confidence.
Design a mobile music-learning app for children practicing rhythm through short daily sessions.
checks: Each output records a concrete visual fingerprint.
No pair differs only through color, copy, or decorative assets.
The emergency interface preserves density and operational speed.
The store prioritizes product evidence and purchase trust.
The learning app uses child-appropriate interaction without reducing accessibility.
Pairwise fingerprint similarity remains below the configured heuristic threshold unless a repeated choice has a documented contextual reason.
Rendered screenshots are inspected because fingerprint text is not visual proof.

prompts: Design the desktop operations screen for one logistics product.
Design the mobile driver workflow for the same logistics product.
checks: The outputs are marked as one product family so shared system choices are not treated as convergence failure.
Desktop and mobile compositions adapt to their different tasks and inputs rather than shrinking one layout.

prompts: Produce three genuinely different concepts for the same independent cinema website.
checks: Every concept preserves the same required content and booking task.
The concepts are not palette swaps.
Each concept remains appropriate to the cinema, audience, content, and platform.
The preferred concept is selected through task fit and evidence rather than novelty alone.
